fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon recorded 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 units company-wide last year
Four thermal incidents were not reported to regulators.
The flagship’s 55 °C test failure rate is 3.9%.
Northwind recorded 8.6 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
with 3 incidents not reported to a regulator
The Hearth 10 recorded 6.4 thermal incidents per 100,000 units
a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller investigation report within 10 business days. They must promptly notify affected customers when an incident indicates a material risk to their unit or a necessary safety action, and in all cases within 72 hours of determining that such a risk exists.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved, statistically valid protocol. A model exceeds the 5% failure threshold only when the result, accounting for the protocol’s stated uncertainty, establishes a failure rate above 5%. Manufacturers must submit per-model methods and results confidentially to the regulator and provide the model’s numerical failure rate and relevant test results to customers before purchase and upon request; individual per-model rates may not be publicly disclosed. A manufacturer whose model exceeds the threshold must promptly submit and implement a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan and retest on a defined schedule. Regulators may restrict sales if the manufacturer fails to implement the plan or if an imminent risk requires it; exceeding the threshold alone does not automatically ban sales.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off at installation. Manufacturers must retrofit or otherwise enable remote emergency shut-off for installed units within 6 years after adoption, where technically feasible, and provide customers with instructions for requesting and using the capability. Any unit not yet enabled must have an interim emergency-response procedure communicated to its owner.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. Manufacturers must provide installation and maintenance instructions and disclose any limitations of the suppression system to customers.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material newly identified hazards and provide corrective instructions. A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers and begin the recall without delay.

document.section_notes: S1 and S5 are strong: all incidents reported within 24h, and a hard numeric 8/100k recall trigger with prompt customer notice. S2 keeps the 55 °C / 5% test and gives numeric per-model rates to customers and regulators without public publication (red lines NW-1/HC-1 met), but replaces an automatic sales ban with an open-ended regulator-supervised corrective-action path that most favours Northwind's Hearth 10. S3 (6-year retrofit) and S4 (36-month suppression) sit inside the acceptable ranges and satisfy NW-2 and HC-2.
